title: StabCF: A Stabilized Training Method for Collaborative Filtering

problem.claim: Sampling-based collaborative-filtering training with implicit feedback suffers from training instability that hinders convergence and causes fluctuating, suboptimal recommendation performance.

gap.claim: Despite the empirical success of sampling-based collaborative-filtering training, its inherent training instability has received little attention.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes training stability in collaborative filtering and identifies noisy or sparse positive samples and inconsistent negative samples as two fundamental sources of instability.
StabCF synthesizes enriched positive samples from historical positives and constructs consistent hard negatives through user-aware negative mixing.
StabCF replaces raw training triplets with synthesized positive-negative pairs to smooth training dynamics and improve convergence stability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on three public datasets significantly stabilize the training process and achieve superior recommendation performance.
The authors report that a PyTorch implementation is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Implicit-feedback collaborative filtering is widely used, and sampling-based training with pairwise ranking losses such as BPR is common.
Training instability in the sampling-based paradigm has received little attention and may hinder convergence and recommendation quality.
The paper attributes instability to noisy or sparse positive samples and inconsistent negative samples.
StabCF addresses these sources by synthesizing enriched positives and constructing consistent hard negatives through user-aware negative mixing.
Experiments on three public datasets are reported to show improved training stability and recommendation performance.

unknowns: The abstract does not name the three public datasets.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, evaluation metrics, or baseline comparisons.
The abstract does not specify the detailed algorithms for positive synthesis or user-aware negative mixing.
The abstract does not report computational costs, sensitivity analyses, or failure cases.
